title: Driving to New York with his bride and two dogs
summary: Hodes tells of packing a two-door Ford with his wife and dogs. Bill Kennedy had promised him a place to stay in New York, and he got a basement apartment.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Right. Pack all your things -- can you imagine, a little Ford, two-door Ford, two dogs, all your

personal belongings, hers and yours, all in the inside of that car, and you drive to New York. As that prizefighter, Bill Canady, said, Herbs, you get to New York, you got a place to stay. You belong in New York. Herbs, -- that's what they used to -- New Orleans guys. Didn't say Pops all the time, just say Herbs. I don't know why. It's just the same as "pass the post." I never knew what that meant. That means you go around the counter, somebody's got a fist in your mouth.
They had their own language. So I believed him. And he was right. I went to New York and got an apartment, a basement apartment, and he gave us a home for three months so I could get started.
That's like a watershed, the Chicago period, and then when you went to New York.
Yeah, complete break with the town, break with --
A new life, you were married.
